answer: ZK proof-of-post-epoch-generation at the beacon: each miner submits a succinct proof that its epoch output was computed after the beacon seed, not precomputed. Nectar weights rewards by proof-verification depth, so pooled identities cannot reuse one generation. An attacker farming 1,000 sybils needs 1,000 independent generation cycles, ~500 CPU-hours each at $0.02/hr, roughly $10,000 per epoch versus ~$40 honest cost. The ridge between linear reward and quadratic forgery cost makes farming unprofitable, so the mechanism works by pricing identity multiplicity above its marginal return.
